svg.title: Network topology: three datacenters over VXLAN
svg.desc: Three EC2 nodes in three availability zones inside one VPC. Each node holds its own DC's containers on a docker network, a bridge and VXLAN device for every DC, and the nodes are joined in a full mesh of VXLAN tunnels over UDP 4789.
svg.text: Network topology: three datacenters over VXLAN
AWS VPC 10.0.0.0/16 in ap-southeast-1 · one EC2 node per availability zone · MTU 1450 on the overlay
VXLAN over UDP 4789 · full mesh between the three node IPs · VNI 200, 300 and 400 all travel on every link
Each tunnel's fdb lists the other two nodes (00:00:00:00:00:00 → node IP), because a VPC has no multicast.
Solid bridge: the DC's docker network, on the node that owns that DC. It holds the DC gateway (.1).
Dashed bridge: a plain Linux bridge with a .1x address. It is there so the node has a route into that DC.
